18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
250	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
251	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
252	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
253	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
254	
255	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
256	
257	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
258	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
259	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
260	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
261	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
262	
263	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
264	
265	提交前必须逐一检查：
266	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
267	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
268	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
269	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
270	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
271	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
272	7. 所有专有名词有定义
273	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
274	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
275	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础
276

# 论文写作风格规范

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

## Worker 操作规范

### ssh-env-setup

# 远程服务器环境搭建规范

## 核心原则

**先探测，再安装。** 不要假设服务器上什么都没有——很多包已经装好了。安装前必须走 discovery 流程。

**镜像快速路径**：连接服务器后，先用 `detect_image` 检测是否为预置镜像。如果是已知镜像且版本匹配，跳过基础环境搭建（Phase 1-4），直接安装项目特有依赖。未检测到镜像时走传统流程。

**aml-train 镜像使用 conda 环境**（不是 venv）。环境激活：`source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base`。pip/python 在 `/root/miniconda3/bin/` 下。**不要假设 .venv 存在，不要创建 venv。**

## Phase 1: 环境探测（用 ssh_read_only）

连接到服务器后，第一步永远是收集信息，不要直接装东西：

```bash
# 1. Python 环境
which python3 && python3 --version
pip3 --version 2>/dev/null || echo "NO_PIP"

# 2. CUDA 环境
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv,noheader 2>/dev/null || echo "NO_GPU"
nvcc --version 2>/dev/null | grep "release" || echo "NO_NVCC"

# 3. 包管理器
ls -d /opt/miniconda3 ~/miniconda3 ~/.conda 2>/dev/null || echo "NO_CONDA"
ls -d .venv venv env 2>/dev/null || echo "NO_VENV"
pip3 list --format=freeze 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "torch|transformers|flash" || echo "NO_ML_PKGS"

# 4. PEP 668 检查
python3 -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_path('stdlib'))" 2>/dev/null
ls /usr/lib/python*/EXTERNALLY-MANAGED 2>/dev/null && echo "PEP668_MANAGED" || echo "PEP668_OK"
```

根据探测结果决定安装策略，不要猜。

## Phase 2: 环境策略选择

根据 Phase 1 结果选择**一个**策略，不要混用：

| 探测结果 | 策略 | 说明 |
|----------|------|------|
| 项目目录有 `.venv/` | 用它：`source .venv/bin/activate` | 最优先 |
| 有 conda 且有写权限 | `conda activate base` 或创建专属 env | 次优先 |
| PEP668_MANAGED + 无 venv | 创建 venv：`python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` | 不要用 --break-system-packages |
| PEP668_OK（无保护） | 直接 `pip install`（旧系统） | 仍建议 venv |

**决不混用 conda install + pip install 到同一环境。** 选了 pip 就全用 pip。

## Phase 3: PyTorch 安装

### CUDA 版本映射（2025-2026 常用）

先从 `nvcc --version` 或 `nvidia-smi` 获取 CUDA 版本，然后匹配：

| CUDA 版本 | PyTorch pip index URL | 推荐 torch 版本 |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| 11.8 | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu118` | ≥ 2.0 |
| 12.1 | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121` | ≥ 2.1 |
| 12.4 | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124` | ≥ 2.4 |
| 12.6 | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126` | ≥ 2.6 |

**不要猜版本号。** 如果不确定可用版本：
```bash
pip index versions torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121 2>/dev/null | head -3
```

安装命令：
```bash
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu{CUDA_SHORT}
```

### 大包超时处理

PyTorch wheel 约 500MB-2GB，默认 SSH 超时可能不够。策略：

```bash
# 方法 1: nohup + 轮询（推荐）
nohup pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121 > /tmp/pip_install.log 2>&1 &
echo $!  # 记录 PID

# 后续用 ssh_read_only 轮询
cat /tmp/pip_install.log | tail -5
ps -p <PID> -o pid= 2>/dev/null && echo "STILL_RUNNING" || echo "DONE"
```

```bash
# 方法 2: 加大 pip 超时
pip install --timeout 300 torch ...
```

## Phase 4: 验证（必须执行）

安装后必须验证，不要假设成功：

```bash
python3 -c "
import torch
print(f'torch={torch.__version__}, cuda={torch.cuda.is_available()}, gpus={torch.cuda.device_count()}')
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    for i in range(torch.cuda.device_count()):
        print(f'  GPU {i}: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(i)} ({torch.cuda.get_device_properties(i).total_mem // 1024**3}GB)')
"
```

验证失败的常见原因：
- `torch.cuda.is_available()` 返回 False → CUDA 版本和 torch 不匹配，重装正确版本
- `ImportError: libcudnn` → 缺 cuDNN，装 `nvidia-cudnn-cu1x`
- GPU 数量不对 → 检查 `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` 环境变量

## Phase 5: 项目依赖

基础环境就绪后，安装项目依赖：

```bash
# 优先用 requirements.txt / pyproject.toml
pip install -r requirements.txt  # 或 pip install -e .

# 常用 ML 依赖补装
pip install transformers datasets einops accelerate wandb
```

flash-attention 特殊处理（编译型包）：
```bash
# 需要匹配的 CUDA toolkit，编译耗时 5-15 分钟
pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation
# 如果编译失败，试预编译版本
pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation 2>/dev/null || pip install flash-attn-wheels
```

## ssh_read_only vs ssh_execute 使用规则

| 操作 | 用哪个工具 |
|------|-----------|
| 检查环境（python --version, nvidia-smi, pip list） | `ssh_read_only` |
| 读文件内容、查日志 | `ssh_read_only` |
| 安装包（pip install, conda install） | `ssh_execute` |
| 创建/修改文件、启动进程 | `ssh_execute` |
| 运行实验脚本 | `ssh_execute` |

**原则：能用 read_only 就用 read_only，只有要改变服务器状态时才用 execute。**

## AutoDL 专项注意事项

AutoDL 实例有一系列特殊约束，5 个项目反复踩坑，必须遵守：

### 磁盘
- **根分区只有 ~30GB，严禁存大文件。** 模型、数据集、HF cache 全部放数据盘 `/root/autodl-tmp/`
- 设置 `HF_HOME=/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache`，否则 HF 默认缓存到根分区导致磁盘满
- 下载模型时用 `--local-dir /root/autodl-tmp/models/<name>`，不要用默认路径

### 网络
- pip install / git clone 前必须 `source /etc/network_turbo` 启用代理加速，否则 pypi.nvidia.com 504 超时、GitHub TLS 断连
- HF 下载设 `HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1`，xet_get 在 AutoDL 上返回 401
- **SSL 证书**：`network_turbo` 的代理使用自签名证书，Python 默认 SSL 验证会失败。必须设置 `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` 和 `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`，否则 HF 下载、datasets 加载等全部报 SSL 错误
- **大模型下载优先用 ModelScope**：AutoDL 代理下载 HuggingFace 大文件极慢（~200KB/s），改用 ModelScope 国内 CDN 速度快很多。`pip install modelscope && python -c "from modelscope import snapshot_download; snapshot_download('Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct', cache_dir='/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache')"`

### SSH
- **AutoDL 实例重启后 SSH 端口会变。** 连接失败时不要反复重试，应提示用户去控制台查新端口并更新 `~/.ssh/config`

content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_8/projects/acr-vla-conformal-refinement/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — ACR-VLA\\n\\n> Last updated: 2026-05-23 | D129: Director 确认 Framing=ACR, 加入 K=2 CRM > K=10 argmin 效率论证\\n\\n---\\n## ⚠️ 最高权限叙述逻辑（用户指定，覆盖一切旧 framing）\\n\\n**论文定位**：Method paper with systematic analysis（不是 analysis paper）\\n\\n### Motivation\\n现有 VLA (Vision-Language-Action) 模型部署后权重冻结，推理时想提升动作质量只有两条路：多次采样选最好的（selection）但开销大，或者用一个轻量模块去修正（correction）。但现有工作（A2C2 解决 temporal staleness、ReconVLA 做 UQ、SC-VLA 用 RL）都没系统回答一个核心问题：推理时的多采样修正到底是什么在起作用？选择还是修正？什么条件下有效，什么条件下会崩？能不能自适应地按需分配推理计算？\\n\\n**我们的回答**：对于 Flow-Matching VLA，提出一种测试时提升的轻量修正模块 CRM，在目标任务上做训练，牺牲一定的时间推理 K 次，利用 Adaptive K 机制和轻量 CRM 进行动作优化，有效提升任务完成率。同时系统分析了多采样修正中选择和修正分别的影响，探讨了修正模块在什么输入条件下有效，在什么条件下会崩。\\n\\n### Method — ACR-VLA Pipeline\\n1. 对 frozen VLA 做 K 次采样，得到 K 个动作候选（默认 K=2）\\n2. Argmin 选最接近均值的候选（centering）\\n3. 轻量 CRM（Conformal Refinement Model, 615K params, 1.8MB）用 VLA observation features 做残差修正\\n4. **Adaptive K 机制**（核心方法贡献）：默认 K=2（batched 推理 ~170ms ≈ K=1），计算两个动作的 L2 距离作为 per-step 不确定性信号。L2 > 阈值 τ（VLA 不确定 → \\\"困难步\\\"）时做 CRM 修正；L2 ≤ τ（VLA 确定 → \\\"简单步\\\"）时直接用 K=2 argmin\\n\\n### Validation — 两个 Flow-Matching VLA 验证（D124: 2-model paper）\\n- **SmolVLA** (0.4B, flow-matching) — 主实验，有充足 CRM 改进空间\\n- **π0.5** (3.6B, flow-matching) — cross-VLA 泛化验证，baseline 饱和（94-99%），CRM 目标 = no-harm\\n\\n每个模型在 LIBERO 四个套件（Object / Spatial / Goal / Long）上统一评估，CRM 在四套件数据上统一训练。\\nOpenVLA-OFT 已放弃（D124: LIBERO 集成 5+ 次修复失败），锁定 2-model paper。\\n\\n### 叙述结构\\n1. **Introduction**: 问题 → 现有方法不足 → 我们提出 ACR-VLA（method + analysis）\\n2. **Method**: ACR-VLA pipeline（CRM 架构 + Adaptive K 机制）\\n3. **Experiments**: 两个 VLA × 四个 benchmark 的全面验证\\n4. **Analysis**: selection vs correction 分解、conditioning-magnitude 交互、适用性边界（作为方法的深入理解，不是独立贡献）\\n5. **Discussion**: 局限性（task-specific、需要 stochastic VLA）、与 A2C2 等的关系\\n\\n### 关键转变（vs 旧 framing）\\n- ❌ 旧：Analysis paper，分析为主，方法为辅\\n- ✅ 新：Method paper，CRM + Adaptive K 为核心贡献，分析为方法的深入验证和理解\\n- ❌ 旧：只在 Object + Spatial 上测\\n- ✅ 新：LIBERO 四套件全测，CRM 在四套件统一训练\\n- ❌ 旧：SmolVLA 为主，其他为补充\\n- ✅ 新：两个 Flow-Matching VLA（SmolVLA 0.4B + π0.5 3.6B）跨规模验证（D124: OFT 已放弃）\\n- ❌ 旧：Title 强调 \\\"Dissecting\\\"\\n- ✅ 新：Title 应强调方法（Adaptive Conformal Refinement / ACR-VLA）\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- **CoRL 2026** (DDL **2026-05-29**)\\n- Framing: Method paper — lightweight test-time correction + adaptive inference-time compute for frozen flow-matching VLAs\\n- Title: TBD（应体现 method 贡献，如 \\\"ACR-VLA: Adaptive Conformal Refinement for Frozen Vision-Language-Action Models\\\"）\\n\\n## Core Insight (D065 revised)\\nLearned correction is the active mechanism that improves frozen VLA policies, but multi-sampling is an enabling condition: it provides a centered starting point within the CRM's bounded correction radius. Neither works alone — K=1 correction performs below baseline (10.3% vs 10.8%), and selection without correction matches baseline. The improvement (+5.8pp, 16.8% vs 10.8%, K=10 n=7 excl. seed42 per D084; K=5: 15.5%) emerges from correction operating on a multi-sample-centered input. Batched inference (D067) eliminates K as a latency factor (~170ms for all K on RTX 4090). The conditioning-magnitude interaction determines success vs catastrophic failure: observation features yield robust corrections (13.4-16.8% across all ε), while conformal per-DOF features cause progressive collapse (14%→0%). This pipeline requires stochastic VLA action diversity as a prerequisite. **D069 boundary**: CRM correction is task-specific — on held-out tasks (LTO), CRM actively degrades VLA (2% vs 14%), revealing that correction quality is bounded by calibration data coverage. Cross-benchmark results (Spatial K=10: 34.5%±1.5%, n=9) are in-distribution (CRM trained on all 20 tasks). **Adaptive K (D076)**: P50 threshold achieves 15.3% at avg_K=3.8 (~91% of fixed K=10). ~~OpenVLA (D087): v2 baseline 69%~~ → D124: OFT 已放弃, 2-model paper.\\n\\n## Headline Metrics\\n> ⚠️ **以下所有绝对 SR 数字来自旧 CRM pipeline（Object+Spatial 数据, wrapper eval）。新 CRM（3-suite unified, wrapper precompute, lerobot-eval baseline）结果待 ~23:00 UTC May 22 训练完成后刷新。** 定性 pattern（correction > selection, magnitude interaction, K-scaling 趋势, latency）预期保持不变。SmolVLA lerobot-eval baseline: Object 66.5%, Spatial 59.5%, Goal 75.5%, Long 50.8%±2.3%。\\n\\n- **K=5 CRM obs_only (PRIMARY, D066)**: 16.0%±2.2% (n=7, seeds 42-48=[14,19,17,15,16,13,18]; JSON-verified) vs VLA-only 10.8%±1.3% (n=9). +4.4pp / ~38% relative. Mann-Whitney U=34.5, rank-biserial r=0.97 (near-perfect separation, seed47=13 ties VLA seed46=13). K=5 vs K=10 primary 待用户确认（K=10 推荐）。\\n- **K=10 CRM obs_only (scaling upper bound)**: 16.8%±1.8% (n=7, excl. seed42 per D084) vs VLA-only 10.8%. +5.8pp / ~53% relative. K=5→K=10 +1.3pp（边际递减）。Statistical tests need recalculation.\\n- **Component decomposition (D064/D070, n=4 update)**: K=10: selection ≈ 0 (argmin 12.3% vs random 11.67%), correction +5.3pp (sole driver). K=5 (n=4): **random 10.5% < VLA-only 11.3%** — 多采样有害！argmin 13.0%±1.6%, selection +1.4pp (32%, borderline), **correction +3.0pp (68%, dominant)**. Correction dominates at ALL K: 68% at K=5, ~100% at K=10. **Cross-benchmark**: Spatial random K=10 = 29.3% (n=3) ≈ VLA-only Spatial 29.3% — multi-sampling无益 pattern consistent across both benchmarks (exp_ids: eval-random-selection-spatial-seed42-r2/seed43/seed44).\\n- **K-value scaling (D063)**: VLA-only 10.8% → CRM K=1(10.3%±1.5%,n=3,NEGATIVE) → CRM K=5(15.5%,n=7) → CRM K=10(16.8%±1.8%,n=7) → CRM K=20(18.7%). K=5 captures ~78% of K=10 benefit over VLA-only. 收益集中在 K=1→K=5 (+5.2pp)，K=5→K=10 +1.3pp（边际递减）\\n- **Magnitude robustness**: obs_only stable 13.4-16.8% all ε (range corrected per Paper Agent audit); perdof collapse 14%→11%→9.9%→4.7%→0%\\n- **Latency (RTX 4090, plan_602 formal)**: ~170ms model inference for all K (~5.5 Hz), full pipeline ~200ms (~5 Hz). CRM overhead 0.246ms, CRM size 1.8MB vs VLA 884MB. Batched inference eliminates K as latency factor.\\n- **Spatial (cross-benchmark, in-distribution)**: K=10 34.5%±1.5% (n=9) vs VLA-only 29.3%±1.7% (n=4). Δ=+5.2pp. Cross-benchmark improvement consistent with Object +5.8pp。Random Selection Spatial K=10: 29.3% (n=3, seed42=34%, seed43=26%, seed44=28%) ≈ VLA-only — correction is sole driver on Spatial too.\\n- **OOD cross-suite (CRM trained on Object+Spatial only)**:\\n  - Goal (OOD, n=4): 67.0% vs VLA-only 69.25%, Δ=-2.25pp, **p=0.42 不显著** — 统计中性。seed44=-9pp 是 outlier，其余 [-2,0,+2]。\\n  - Long (OOD, n=4): 17.5% vs VLA-only 13.25%(paired), Δ=+4.25pp — 正面但改善集中于 microwave task\\n  - LTO (within-suite OOD, D069): 2% vs 14%, Δ=-12pp — **灾难性**\\n  - **OOD 图景**: cross-suite OOD 中性(Goal)到正面(Long)，within-suite held-out 灾难性(LTO)。CRM 校正模式可跨 suite 迁移但不能迁移到同 suite 未见 task。\\n- **Cross-VLA boundary**: OpenVLA v1=0% → **v2=69%** (D087, 10 trials/task). CRM obs_only training complete (plan_802, val_loss=0.077260). CRM eval pending GPU. SmolVLA naturally stochastic; OpenVLA near-deterministic at T=0.5 (8/10 identical actions).\\n- **Adaptive K (D076→D090)**: K=2 L2 pairwise distance ρ=0.9979 vs K=10 variance. **P50 threshold: 15.3% SR at avg_K=3.8 (~91% of fixed K=10, 38% compute)**. D088 Learned Uncertainty Head NO-GO (mean 12.0% < VLA-only). D090 Plan A (K=2 conformal + selective CRM) in progress.\\n\\n## Core Claims (3 claims, D061)\\n\\n### C1: Dissecting inference-time correction — correction is active mechanism, multi-sampling is enabling condition\\n- K VLA samples → argmin(L2 to mean) → learned MLP residual correction with observation features\\n- 16.8%±1.8% vs 10.8%±1.3% VLA-only (n=7 vs n=9, excl. seed42 per D084; statistical tests need recalculation with updated data); vs argmin 12.3%\\n- Component decomposition (D064): argmin selection ≈ random (12.3% vs 11.67%, n=3, not significant). CRM correction +5.2pp over argmin, +5.8pp over random. Multi-sampling alone (random K=10) ≈ VLA-only — correction is the active mechanism\\n- **Spatial cross-benchmark validation**: Random Selection Spatial K=10 = 29.3% (n=3, seed42=34%, seed43=26%, seed44=28%; exp_ids: eval-random-selection-spatial-seed42-r2, eval-random-selection-spatial-seed43, eval-random-selection-spatial-seed44) ≈ VLA-only Spatial 29.3% (n=4). CRM K=10 Spatial: 34.5% → correction Δ=+5.2pp. Pattern consistent with Object: multi-sampling alone ≈ VLA-only on both benchmarks, correction is the sole driver (+5.8pp Object, +5.2pp Spatial)\\n- K-value scaling (D063): CRM K=1(10.3%,n=3) → CRM K=5(15.5%,n=7) → CRM K=10(16.8%,n=7). VLA-only baseline = 10.8% (K=1, no CRM). K=5 captures ~78% of K=10 benefit over VLA-only. CRM K=1→K=5 +5.2pp, K=5→K=10 +1.3pp\\n- CRM K=1 does NOT work (10.3% < VLA-only 10.8%) — correction without multi-sample centering is harmful. Same CRM trained on K=10 data; K=1 failure = input distribution shift outside bounded correction radius\\n- CRM is a correction module (not selection/ranking): obs_only CRM does NOT use conformal features (D058)\\n- Evidence: Table 1 (component decomposition), Figure 3 (K-value curve)\\n\\n### C2: Conditioning-magnitude interaction — first systematic study\\n- Same CRM architecture, same training, only conditioning features differ → stable vs catastrophic failure\\n- obs_only (observation features only): 13.4-16.8% stable across all ε (n=1-7 per point, range corrected)\\n- perdof (per-DOF conformal features): 14%→11%→9.9%→4.7%→0% dose-response collapse\\n- perdof default (uncapped): 0% × 5 data points (catastrophic collapse, all seeds consistent)\\n- Root cause: rank-deficient covariance in high-D action space → noisy directional signals amplified by magnitude\\n- Practical takeaway: bounded magnitude + observation features = necessary conditions for safe correction\\n- Evidence: Figure 2 (magnitude curves), Section analysis\\n\\n### C3: Applicability boundaries — two prerequisites + unified failure framework (updated with OOD cross-suite)\\n- **Prerequisite 1: VLA diversity** — stochastic multi-sampling → action diversity across K samples. OpenVLA (7B, tokenized): T=0.5 produces 8/10 identical actions, near-deterministic (D087: v2 baseline=69%, CRM eval pending to test if correction works despite low diversity). SmolVLA (0.4B, flow-matching): naturally stochastic.\\n- **Prerequisite 2: Task proximity in CRM training data** — CRM learns task-specific correction biases. OOD behavior is **proximity-dependent**:\\n  - Near-OOD (within-suite held-out, LTO): same manipulation structure, different objects/goals → CRM \\\"recognizes\\\" context but correction direction is wrong → **adversarial** (-12pp, 2% vs 14%)\\n  - Far-OOD (cross-suite, Goal/Long): different observation distribution → correction signal naturally decays → **neutral** (Goal -1.6pp p=0.46) or **primitive-level transfer** (Long +3.3pp p=0.046, driven by microwave task sharing pick-and-place primitives with training data)\\n- **Unified failure framework** — CRM correction = bounded task-specific residual, sensitive to three distribution shifts:\\n  - Input shift (K=1): single sample ≠ multi-sample mean → correction points wrong direction (10.3% < baseline)\\n  - Task shift (proximity-dependent): near-OOD → adversarial perturbation (LTO -12pp); far-OOD → null operation (Goal ±2pp) or primitive transfer (Long +3.3pp)\\n  - Feature shift (perdof, C2): noisy conformal signals amplified by magnitude → catastrophic collapse (→0%)\\n- This is the central boundary analysis — three failure modes with mechanistic explanations. Near-OOD more dangerous than far-OOD parallels ML adversarial robustness literature.\\n- Evidence: Figure 4 (action diversity), LTO data, Goal/Long cross-suite data, magnitude curves (C2)\\n- **Long per-task breakdown required**: microwave task contributes majority of improvement. Report overall SR (honest) + per-task table. Discuss primitive-level transfer mechanism.\\n\\n## D072/D076: Adaptive K — K=2 L2 Probe 机制（用户硬要求，已验证）\\n\\n⚠️ **固定 K=10 暴力多推理不可接受**。Adaptive K 信号已验证：K=2 L2 pairwise distance。\\n\\n**信号验证结果 (D076)**:\\n- **K=2 L2 vs K=10 variance: ρ=0.9979** — 近乎完美替代，2 次推理预测 10 次推理的不确定性\\n- FMVD (flow turbulence): ρ=0.0825 → NO-GO (D075). 测量不同维度的不确定性，与 action variance 无关\\n- K=2 L2 vs FMVD: ρ=0.09 — 两个信号完全独立\\n\\n**确定的架构**:\\n- 默认 K=2（batched推理，延迟=K=1 ~170ms）\\n- 计算 K=2 pairwise L2 distance 作为 per-step 不确定性信号\\n- L2 > τ → 扩展到 K=10 + argmin + CRM obs_only 校正（\\\"困难步\\\"）\\n- L2 ≤ τ → K=2 均值，不过 CRM（\\\"简单步\\\"）\\n- 阈值 τ 从校准数据 percentile 选取：P25=0.055, P50=0.075, P75=0.099, P90=0.127\\n\\n**Phase 2 结果 (Object)**:\\n- **P50 (τ=0.075): 15.3% SR at avg_K=3.8 — ~91% of K=10 (16.8%) at 38% compute** ← 推荐默认\\n- P25/P75/P90 阈值 sweep 完成，Pareto 曲线可用\\n- Spatial 跨 benchmark 验证完成\\n\\n**对论文 framing 的影响**:\\n- 从纯 analysis paper 升级为 analysis + method paper\\n- 分析 (correction > selection, magnitude interaction, boundaries) 作为 FOUNDATION → 指导 adaptive 机制设计\\n- K=10 固定推理保留为 oracle upper bound\\n- FMVD NO-GO 作为 negative result / ablation（ODE-space 信号 vs action-space 信号）\\n- 新增贡献 C4：adaptive inference-time compute allocation for VLA\\n\\n## D088→D090: Adaptive K 方法路径（2026-05-20）\\n\\n**D088 Learned Uncertainty Head — NO-GO**:\\n- 方案 B: 3-layer MLP (960→16→16→1, 15,665 params) 在 VLA-expert deviation 上训练，AUC=0.8131, F1=0.7674, τ=0.42\\n- 3 seed eval: mean SR=12.0% < VLA-only baseline (10.8%→14%) — 方法有害\\n- 根因: avg_k≈1.0, uncertainty head 几乎从不触发 CRM correction\\n- 结论: offline uncertainty classification 不如 online multi-sample divergence\\n\\n**D090 Plan A: K=2 Conformal + Selective CRM — IN PROGRESS**:\\n- K=2 forward → L2 pairwise distance as uncertainty → if L2 > τ(P50=0.074855): argmin-to-centroid + CRM correction; else: argmin-to-centroid only\\n- 与 D076 adaptive K 的区别: Plan A 在 K=2 就做 CRM correction（不扩展到 K=10），更实用但可能牺牲性能\\n- 代码已实现 (`adaptive_conformal_crm` mode in evaluate.py)，3 seed eval 待 GPU 释放部署\\n- Safety net: Adaptive K P50 已有 15.3% 结果可用\\n\\n**方案 C (Action Distribution Geometry)**: 备选，如 Plan A 也失败则启用\\n\\n**D129 效率论证 (Director insight, 2026-05-23)**:\\n- **Adaptive CRM K=2: 81% SR on Spatial > ReconVLA K=10: 79% SR (+2pp)**\\n- K=2 + CRM correction (327K params, 1次小模型推理) > K=10 argmin selection (10次VLA推理)\\n- **论文 story 核心**: \\\"你不需要 K=10 次推理来选好 action，K=2 + 学习到的 CRM 修正就够了\\\"\\n- 效率 + 效果双赢，不是 marginal contribution\\n- Ablation table 坦诚展示各组件贡献（K-selection vs CRM correction vs adaptive gating）\\n- **待 threshold sweep (tau=0.15/0.25/0.35) 结果确定 adaptive gating 叙事强度**\\n\\n**对论文影响 (D091, updated D129)**:\\n- 核心 claims (C1-C3) 不受影响 — D088 作为 rejected alternative 写入 Discussion\\n- D090 成功: 替代 D076 adaptive K 作为 method contribution\\n- D090 失败: D076 adaptive K P50=15.3% 结果作为 safety net\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n- **Problem**: Frozen VLA deployment with a lightweight learned correction module can improve success rates — but fixed multi-sampling (K=10) is computationally wasteful. When does correction actually help, and can we allocate inference-time compute adaptively?\\n- **Gap**: No systematic study of (1) what drives effective learned corrections for VLA, (2) how to adaptively allocate inference-time compute based on per-step uncertainty, (3) when multi-sample correction helps vs fails across VLA architectures. Existing methods (A2C2: temporal correction; ReconVLA: UQ; SC-VLA: residual RL) address adjacent problems.\\n- **Our angle**: We first dissect inference-time multi-sample correction, finding that learned correction is the active mechanism while multi-sampling is an enabling condition. These findings inform the design of an **adaptive K mechanism** that dynamically allocates compute — sampling more only when the VLA is uncertain. The conditioning-magnitude interaction and applicability boundaries further constrain safe deployment.\\n- **Headline**: \\\"K=2 + learned CRM correction (327K params) beats K=10 argmin selection (81% vs 79% on Spatial) — 2 VLA inferences + 1 lightweight correction > 10 VLA inferences. Correction is the active mechanism, not selection. Adaptive gating selectively applies CRM only on uncertain steps. Efficiency + effectiveness dual win.\\\"\\n\\n## Competitive Landscape\\n\\n### A2C2 (D060) — Complementary, not competing\\nFrozen VLA + per-step correction within action chunks. Solves **temporal staleness** (chunk actions become outdated during execution). Our method solves **initial action quality** (improve the action before execution). Orthogonal and combinable. A2C2 trains SmolVLA from scratch (67-72% baseline) — different setting from our frozen pretrained VLA (10.8%).\\n\\n### ReconVLA — Same domain, different route\\nConformal quantile regression for UQ + OOD detection on frozen VLA. Does not perform learned correction.\\n\\n### SC-VLA / PLD — RL-based refinement\\nResidual RL per-task. Requires online training, not plug-and-play. PLD achieves 99% on LIBERO but with full fine-tuning.\\n\\n### Our positioning (D058/D061, updated D072)\\nFirst to (1) decompose inference-time VLA correction into selection vs correction contributions, (2) systematically study conditioning-magnitude interaction revealing catastrophic failure mode, (3) establish applicability boundaries across VLA architectures (stochastic vs deterministic), **(4) propose adaptive inference-time compute allocation based on per-step uncertainty — dynamically deciding K rather than fixed brute-force sampling**. The adaptive K mechanism connects to LLM inference-time compute scaling trends in embodied AI.\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n1. **\\\"Absolute performance is low (16.8% on an 11% baseline)\\\"**\\n   - Response: This is frozen fine-tuned VLA with inference-time correction (VLA weights fixed during CRM training and deployment). ~53% relative improvement (+5.8pp) is significant given the frozen constraint. The contribution is the systematic analysis of when/why/how inference-time correction works, not SOTA absolute numbers. Community benchmark: A2C2 trains SmolVLA from scratch on LIBERO reaching 67-72%, a different training regime.\\n\\n2. **\\\"Method only works for weak/small VLAs\\\"**\\n   - Response: Honest analysis (C3). Correction value correlates inversely with base model quality/determinism. This is a genuine insight with practical implications: small stochastic VLAs are relevant for edge deployment, latency-constrained scenarios, and new task generalization without fine-tuning.\\n\\n3. **\\\"K=1 doesn't work, K=10 needs 10× compute\\\"**\\n   - Response: **Adaptive K (D076) directly addresses this.** Default K=2 (same latency as K=1 with batching ~170ms). K=2 pairwise L2 distance as uncertainty signal (ρ=0.9979 vs K=10 variance). High uncertainty → extend to K=10 + CRM; low uncertainty → use K=2 directly. avg_K=3.8, achieving ~91% of fixed K=10 performance (15.3% vs 16.8%). K=1 CRM failure (10.3%) is a finding: correction needs multi-sample centering. FMVD failure (ρ=0.08) is ablation evidence for why action-space signals work while ODE-space signals don't.\\n\\n4. **\\\"obs_only is just a residual MLP, where is the novelty?\\\"**\\n   - Response: Novelty is the systematic analysis, not the architecture. Architecture simplicity isolates the conditioning signal's effect. The conditioning-magnitude interaction and component decomposition are new.\\n\\n5. **\\\"Single benchmark (LIBERO-Object)\\\"**\\n   - Response: **Fully addressed with LIBERO-Spatial data.** CRM K=10 Spatial: 35.0%±1.0% (n=3) vs VLA-only 29.3%±1.7% (n=4). Paired Δ=+5.7pp (n=3), matching Object's +6pp. K=5 Spatial: 33.5% (n=2). Both Object and Spatial are in-distribution (CRM trained on all 20 tasks). LTO (D069) shows OOD limitation — honest boundary. OpenVLA v2=69% baseline (D087), CRM eval pending.\\n\\n6. **\\\"Why does per-DOF fail?\\\"**\\n   - Response: K samples in 7D action space → rank-deficient covariance → noisy directional signals. Low ε masks noise; high ε amplifies it. 3 seeds × 0% at uncapped confirms catastrophic failure.\\n\\n7. **\\\"A2C2 does K=1 correction and it works, yours doesn't\\\"**\\n   - Response (D060): A2C2 solves temporal staleness (within-chunk correction with new observations), not initial action quality. Different problem, different mechanism. Our K=1 failure is about single-sample residual correction without temporal context — complementary finding.\\n\\n8. **\\\"Why not just fine-tune the VLA?\\\"**\\n   - Response: VLA is already fine-tuned (LoRA SFT on LIBERO), but inference-time correction provides additional gains without modifying VLA weights. ### Motivation
现有 VLA (Vision-Language-Action) 模型部署后权重冻结，推理时想提升动作质量只有两条路：多次采样选最好的（selection）但开销大，或者用一个轻量模块去修正（correction）。但现有工作（A2C2 解决 temporal staleness、ReconVLA 做 UQ、SC-VLA 用 RL）都没系统回答一个核心问题：推理时的多采样修正到底是什么在起作用？选择还是修正？什么条件下有效，什么条件下会崩？能不能自适应地按需分配推理计算？

**我们的回答**：对于 Flow-Matching VLA，提出一种测试时提升的轻量修正模块 CRM，在目标任务上做训练，牺牲一定的时间推理 K 次，利用 Adaptive K 机制和轻量 CRM 进行动作优化，有效提升任务完成率。同时系统分析了多采样修正中选择和修正分别的影响，探讨了修正模块在什么输入条件下有效，在什么条件下会崩。

### Method — ACR-VLA Pipeline
1. 对 frozen VLA 做 K 次采样，得到 K 个动作候选（默认 K=2）
2. Argmin 选最接近均值的候选（centering）
3. 轻量 CRM（Conformal Refinement Model, 615K params, 1.8MB）用 VLA observation features 做残差修正
4. **Adaptive K 机制**（核心方法贡献）：默认 K=2（batched 推理 ~170ms ≈ K=1），计算两个动作的 L2 距离作为 per-step 不确定性信号。L2 > 阈值 τ（VLA 不确定 → "困难步"）时做 CRM 修正；L2 ≤ τ（VLA 确定 → "简单步"）时直接用 K=2 argmin

### Validation — 两个 Flow-Matching VLA 验证（D124: 2-model paper）
- **SmolVLA** (0.4B, flow-matching) — 主实验，有充足 CRM 改进空间
- **π0.5** (3.6B, flow-matching) — cross-VLA 泛化验证，baseline 饱和（94-99%），CRM 目标 = no-harm

每个模型在 LIBERO 四个套件（Object / Spatial / Goal / Long）上统一评估，CRM 在四套件数据上统一训练。
OpenVLA-OFT 已放弃（D124: LIBERO 集成 5+ 次修复失败），锁定 2-model paper。

## Core Insight (D065 revised)
Learned correction is the active mechanism that improves frozen VLA policies, but multi-sampling is an enabling condition: it provides a centered starting point within the CRM's bounded correction radius. Neither works alone — K=1 correction performs below baseline (10.3% vs 10.8%), and selection without correction matches baseline. The improvement (+5.8pp, 16.8% vs 10.8%, K=10 n=7 excl. seed42 per D084; K=5: 15.5%) emerges from correction operating on a multi-sample-centered input. Batched inference (D067) eliminates K as a latency factor (~170ms for all K on RTX 4090). The conditioning-magnitude interaction determines success vs catastrophic failure: observation features yield robust corrections (13.4-16.8% across all ε), while conformal per-DOF features cause progressive collapse (14%→0%). This pipeline requires stochastic VLA action diversity as a prerequisite. **D069 boundary**: CRM correction is task-specific — on held-out tasks (LTO), CRM actively degrades VLA (2% vs 14%), revealing that correction quality is bounded by calibration data coverage. Cross-benchmark results (Spatial K=10: 34.5%±1.5%, n=9) are in-distribution (CRM trained on all 20 tasks). **Adaptive K (D076)**: P50 threshold achieves 15.3% at avg_K=3.8 (~91% of fixed K=10). ~~OpenVLA (D087): v2 baseline 69%~~ → D124: OFT 已放弃, 2-model paper.

## Core Claims (3 claims, D061)

### C1: Dissecting inference-time correction — correction is active mechanism, multi-sampling is enabling condition
- K VLA samples → argmin(L2 to mean) → learned MLP residual correction with observation features
- 16.8%±1.8% vs 10.8%±1.3% VLA-only (n=7 vs n=9, excl. seed42 per D084; statistical tests need recalculation with updated data); vs argmin 12.3%
- Component decomposition (D064): argmin selection ≈ random (12.3% vs 11.67%, n=3, not significant). CRM correction +5.2pp over argmin, +5.8pp over random. Multi-sampling alone (random K=10) ≈ VLA-only — correction is the active mechanism
- **Spatial cross-benchmark validation**: Random Selection Spatial K=10 = 29.3% (n=3, seed42=34%, seed43=26%, seed44=28%; exp_ids: eval-random-selection-spatial-seed42-r2, eval-random-selection-spatial-seed43, eval-random-selection-spatial-seed44) ≈ VLA-only Spatial 29.3% (n=4). CRM K=10 Spatial: 34.5% → correction Δ=+5.2pp. Pattern consistent with Object: multi-sampling alone ≈ VLA-only on both benchmarks, correction is the sole driver (+5.8pp Object, +5.2pp Spatial)
- K-value scaling (D063): CRM K=1(10.3%,n=3) → CRM K=5(15.5%,n=7) → CRM K=10(16.8%,n=7). VLA-only baseline = 10.8% (K=1, no CRM). K=5 captures ~78% of K=10 benefit over VLA-only. CRM K=1→K=5 +5.2pp, K=5→K=10 +1.3pp
- CRM K=1 does NOT work (10.3% < VLA-only 10.8%) — correction without multi-sample centering is harmful. Same CRM trained on K=10 data; K=1 failure = input distribution shift outside bounded correction radius
- CRM is a correction module (not selection/ranking): obs_only CRM does NOT use conformal features (D058)
- Evidence: Table 1 (component decomposition), Figure 3 (K-value curve)

### C2: Conditioning-magnitude interaction — first systematic study
- Same CRM architecture, same training, only conditioning features differ → stable vs catastrophic failure
- obs_only (observation features only): 13.4-16.8% stable across all ε (n=1-7 per point, range corrected)
- perdof (per-DOF conformal features): 14%→11%→9.9%→4.7%→0% dose-response collapse
- perdof default (uncapped): 0% × 5 data points (catastrophic collapse, all seeds consistent)
- Root cause: rank-deficient covariance in high-D action space → noisy directional signals amplified by magnitude
- Practical takeaway: bounded magnitude + observation features = necessary conditions for safe correction
- Evidence: Figure 2 (magnitude curves), Section analysis

### C3: Applicability boundaries — two prerequisites + unified failure framework (updated with OOD cross-suite)
- **Prerequisite 1: VLA diversity** — stochastic multi-sampling → action diversity across K samples. OpenVLA (7B, tokenized): T=0.5 produces 8/10 identical actions, near-deterministic (D087: v2 baseline=69%, CRM eval pending to test if correction works despite low diversity). SmolVLA (0.4B, flow-matching): naturally stochastic.
- **Prerequisite 2: Task proximity in CRM training data** — CRM learns task-specific correction biases. OOD behavior is **proximity-dependent**:
  - Near-OOD (within-suite held-out, LTO): same manipulation structure, different objects/goals → CRM "recognizes" context but correction direction is wrong → **adversarial** (-12pp, 2% vs 14%)
  - Far-OOD (cross-suite, Goal/Long): different observation distribution → correction signal naturally decays → **neutral** (Goal -1.6pp p=0.46) or **primitive-level transfer** (Long +3.3pp p=0.046, driven by microwave task sharing pick-and-place primitives with training data)
- **Unified failure framework** — CRM correction = bounded task-specific residual, sensitive to three distribution shifts:
  - Input shift (K=1): single sample ≠ multi-sample mean → correction points wrong direction (10.3% < baseline)
  - Task shift (proximity-dependent): near-OOD → adversarial perturbation (LTO -12pp); far-OOD → null operation (Goal ±2pp) or primitive transfer (Long +3.3pp)
  - Feature shift (perdof, C2): noisy conformal signals amplified by magnitude → catastrophic collapse (→0%)
- This is the central boundary analysis — three failure modes with mechanistic explanations. Near-OOD more dangerous than far-OOD parallels ML adversarial robustness literature.
- Evidence: Figure 4 (action diversity), LTO data, Goal/Long cross-suite data, magnitude curves (C2)
- **Long per-task breakdown required**: microwave task contributes majority of improvement. Report overall SR (honest) + per-task table. Discuss primitive-level transfer mechanism.

**信号验证结果 (D076)**:
- **K=2 L2 vs K=10 variance: ρ=0.9979** — 近乎完美替代，2 次推理预测 10 次推理的不确定性

- 默认 K=2（batched推理，延迟=K=1 ~170ms）

- L2 > τ → 扩展到 K=10 + argmin + CRM obs_only 校正（"困难步"）
- L2 ≤ τ → K=2 均值，不过 CRM（"简单步"）

## Story Spine
- **Problem**: Frozen VLA deployment with a lightweight learned correction module can improve success rates — but fixed multi-sampling (K=10) is computationally wasteful. When does correction actually help, and can we allocate inference-time compute adaptively?
- **Gap**: No systematic study of (1) what drives effective learned corrections for VLA, (2) how to adaptively allocate inference-time compute based on per-step uncertainty, (3) when multi-sample correction helps vs fails across VLA architectures. Existing methods (A2C2: temporal correction; ReconVLA: UQ; SC-VLA: residual RL) address adjacent problems.
- **Our angle**: We first dissect inference-time multi-sample correction, finding that learned correction is the active mechanism while multi-sampling is an enabling condition. These findings inform the design of an **adaptive K mechanism** that dynamically allocates compute — sampling more only when the VLA is uncertain. The conditioning-magnitude interaction and applicability boundaries further constrain safe deployment.
- **Headline**: "K=2 + learned CRM correction (327K params) beats K=10 argmin selection (81% vs 79% on Spatial) — 2 VLA inferences + 1 lightweight correction > 10 VLA inferences. Correction is the active mechanism, not selection. Adaptive gating selectively applies CRM only on uncertain steps. Efficiency + effectiveness dual win."

## Competitive Landscape

### A2C2 (D060) — Complementary, not competing
Frozen VLA + per-step correction within action chunks. Solves **temporal staleness** (chunk actions become outdated during execution). Our method solves **initial action quality** (improve the action before execution). Orthogonal and combinable. A2C2 trains SmolVLA from scratch (67-72% baseline) — different setting from our frozen pretrained VLA (10.8%).

### ReconVLA — Same domain, different route
Conformal quantile regression for UQ + OOD detection on frozen VLA. Does not perform learned correction.

### SC-VLA / PLD — RL-based refinement
Residual RL per-task. Requires online training, not plug-and-play. PLD achieves 99% on LIBERO but with full fine-tuning.

### Our positioning (D058/D061, updated D072)
First to (1) decompose inference-time VLA correction into selection vs correction contributions, (2) systematically study conditioning-magnitude interaction revealing catastrophic failure mode, (3) establish applicability boundaries across VLA architectures (stochastic vs deterministic), **(4) propose adaptive inference-time compute allocation based on per-step uncertainty — dynamically deciding K rather than fixed brute-force sampling**. The adaptive K mechanism connects to LLM inference-time compute scaling trends in embodied AI.

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

1. **"Absolute performance is low (16.8% on an 11% baseline)"**
   - Response: This is frozen fine-tuned VLA with inference-time correction (VLA weights fixed during CRM training and deployment). ~53% relative improvement (+5.8pp) is significant given the frozen constraint. The contribution is the systematic analysis of when/why/how inference-time correction works, not SOTA absolute numbers. Community benchmark: A2C2 trains SmolVLA from scratch on LIBERO reaching 67-72%, a different training regime.

2. **"Method only works for weak/small VLAs"**
   - Response: Honest analysis (C3). Correction value correlates inversely with base model quality/determinism. This is a genuine insight with practical implications: small stochastic VLAs are relevant for edge deployment, latency-constrained scenarios, and new task generalization without fine-tuning.

3. **"K=1 doesn't work, K=10 needs 10× compute"**
   - Response: **Adaptive K (D076) directly addresses this.** Default K=2 (same latency as K=1 with batching ~170ms). K=2 pairwise L2 distance as uncertainty signal (ρ=0.9979 vs K=10 variance). High uncertainty → extend to K=10 + CRM; low uncertainty → use K=2 directly. avg_K=3.8, achieving ~91% of fixed K=10 performance (15.3% vs 16.8%). K=1 CRM failure (10.3%) is a finding: correction needs multi-sample centering. FMVD failure (ρ=0.08) is ablation evidence for why action-space signals work while ODE-space signals don't.

4. **"obs_only is just a residual MLP, where is the novelty?"**
   - Response: Novelty is the systematic analysis, not the architecture. Architecture simplicity isolates the conditioning signal's effect. The conditioning-magnitude interaction and component decomposition are new.

5. **"Single benchmark (LIBERO-Object)"**
   - Response: **Fully addressed with LIBERO-Spatial data.** CRM K=10 Spatial: 35.0%±1.0% (n=3) vs VLA-only 29.3%±1.7% (n=4). Paired Δ=+5.7pp (n=3), matching Object's +6pp. K=5 Spatial: 33.5% (n=2). Both Object and Spatial are in-distribution (CRM trained on all 20 tasks). LTO (D069) shows OOD limitation — honest boundary. OpenVLA v2=69% baseline (D087), CRM eval pending.

6. **"Why does per-DOF fail?"**
   - Response: K samples in 7D action space → rank-deficient covariance → noisy directional signals. Low ε masks noise; high ε amplifies it. 3 seeds × 0% at uncapped confirms catastrophic failure.

7. **"A2C2 does K=1 correction and it works, yours doesn't"**
   - Response (D060): A2C2 solves temporal staleness (within-chunk correction with new observations), not initial action quality. Different problem, different mechanism. Our K=1 failure is about single-sample residual correction without temporal context — complementary finding.

8. **"Why not just fine-tune the VLA?"**
   - Response: VLA is already fine-tuned (LoRA SFT on LIBERO), but inference-time correction provides additional gains without modifying VLA weights. CRM does not modify VLA weights but requires VLA rollout cache on deployment tasks for CRM training. LTO (D069) confirms: CRM correction is task-specific — deployment tasks must be covered in CRM training data.

27	**Figure**: Fig. 1 — Pipeline overview diagram (sample → conformal selection → CRM correction → execution)

31	## 2. Related Work (~1.5 pages)

33	→ See `paper/sections/related_work.md` for full draft.
34	
35	Three subsections:
36	- (a) VLA Robustness and Inference-Time Adaptation
37	- (b) Conformal Prediction in Robotics

40	---
41	
42	## 3. Method (~2 pages)
43	
44	### 3.1 Problem Setup and Notation
45	- Frozen VLA policy π_θ generating K action samples via flow matching
46	- Distribution shift setting: train on nominal env, deploy under perturbation (LIBERO-Plus object/spatial)
47	- Goal: inference-time module that improves closed-loop success without retraining π_θ
48	
49	### 3.2 Conformal Sample Selection
50	- Generate K=10 action samples from flow-matching VLA
51	- Compute nonconformity scores (CGS-based Mahalanobis scoring [Braun et al., 2025])
52	- Select best sample via argmin nonconformity score
53	- This stage approximates ReconVLA's selection strategy — serves as our primary baseline
54	
55	**Key refs**: [Angelopoulos & Bates, 2023], [Braun et al., 2025], [Chen et al., 2026]

60	- **CRM Variants** (systematic ablation):

73	- Hypothesis: per-DOF features produce overconfident directional corrections that compound at high magnitude

| obs_only 0.2 | 18.0% (5/10) | +6.0pp | running |
| argmin K=10 | 12.0% | baseline | `eval-argmin-only-object` |
| VLA-only K=1 | 12.0% | 0pp | `eval-vla-only-object-k1` |
| VLA-mean K=10 | 12.0% | 0pp | — |
| perdof 0.1 | 11.0% | -1.0pp | `eval-acr-object-v4-small` |
| scalar 0.1 | 9.0% | -3.0pp | `eval-acr-object-v4-scalar` |

**Key message**: obs_only CRM is the only method that significantly improves over sample selection. Per-DOF conformal features and scalar scores fail to provide useful correction signal.

**Figure**: Fig. 3 — Bar chart comparing all 6 methods on object benchmark (with error bars from seed=43)

### 4.3 Spatial Manipulation: An Honest Negative Result

**Table 2**: Spatial benchmark 10-task success rates (LOCKED)

| Method | SR | Δ vs argmin | exp_id |
|--------|-----|-------------|--------|
| obs_only 0.1 | 35% | +1pp | `eval-acr-spatial-v4-obs-only-r3` |
| perdof 0.1 | 35% | +1pp | `eval-acr-spatial-v4-small-r2` |
| argmin K=10 | 34% | baseline | `eval-argmin-only-spatial-r2` |
| scalar 0.1 | 32% | -2pp | `eval-acr-spatial-v4-scalar` |
| VLA-mean K=10 | 32% | -2pp | — |
| VLA-only K=1 | 30% | -4pp | — |

**Key message**: No CRM variant helps on spatial tasks. Hypothesis: spatial perturbation (position offset) causes fundamentally different error modes that action correction cannot address — requires re-planning, not action refinement. Object substitution creates correctable action distribution shifts.

### 4.4 Correction Magnitude Sensitivity (Key Empirical Contribution)

**Table 3 / Figure**: Magnitude sweep on spatial (4 norm values × 2 CRM variants)

| norm | obs_only SR | perdof SR | gap | exp_id |
|------|------------|-----------|-----|--------|
| 0.03 | 55.0% (4t) | 30.0% (10t) | +25pp* | magnitude sweep D032 |
| 0.05 | 35.0% (10t) | 31.0% (10t) | +4.0pp | `eval-mag-obsonly-norm005` |
| 0.2 | 35.0% (10t) | 28.3% (6t) | +6.7pp | `eval-mag-obsonly-norm02` |
| 0.3 | 36.0% (10t) | 26.0% (10t) | +10pp | `eval-mag-perdof-norm03` |

**Figure**: Fig. 4 — Line plot: SR vs correction norm for obs_only and perdof. obs_only flat, perdof declining.

**Key message**: obs_only CRM maintains stable performance across 10× range of correction magnitudes. perdof CRM collapses at high norm → overconfident directional corrections from noisy per-DOF features.

### 4.5 K-Value Sweep Ablation

→ See `paper/sections/ablation_k_sweep.md` for full draft.

**Key message**: K=2 (Plan A) ≈ K=10 ≈ K=20 on both Object (18.3% / 16.8% / 18.8%) and Spatial (35.0% / 34.5% / 34.3%). Diminishing returns beyond K=2 justify Plan A (adaptive K=2) as Pareto-optimal — matches K=20 SR with ≤2× VLA compute. K=20 exp_ids: `eval-k20-obs-only-object-seed{42,43,44,45}`, `eval-k20-obs-only-spatial-seed{42,43,44}`.

### 4.6 Statistical Significance (seed=43 results, pending)
- Fisher exact test on combined 200 trials (2 seeds × 10 tasks × 10 rollouts)
- Per-task breakdown showing consistency
- Bootstrap 95% CI for success rate differences

---

## 5. Discussion (~0.5 pages)

### Why obs_only works and perdof doesn't
- Observation embeddings encode task-relevant semantic information (object identity, spatial layout) that is stable across distribution shifts
- Per-DOF conformal statistics estimated from K=10 samples are noisy — covariance estimation from 10 samples in 7D action space is ill-conditioned
- Magnitude sweep evidence: perdof collapses at high norm = CRM learns overconfident corrections from noisy per-DOF features; obs_only corrections remain conservative/stable
- Connection to literature: [Ovadia et al., 2019] show UQ degrades under shift; [Sampson et al., 2024] show per-dimension marginal CP loses inter-DOF coherence

### Limitations
- Simulation only (LIBERO); real-robot transfer untested
- SmolVLA backbone only; generalization to other VLAs (OpenVLA, pi0) untested
- Spatial tasks show no improvement — CRM cannot address perturbations requiring re-planning
- CRM trained per-benchmark (not zero-shot); requires calibration data from target distribution

### Future Work
- Real-robot experiments
- Adaptive magnitude scheduling (decay over episode, uncertainty-conditioned)
- Combining with training-time robustness methods (SRPO, RobustVLA)
- Multi-VLA evaluation

---

## 6. Conclusion (~0.25 pages)
- First systematic study of inference-time learned action correction for frozen VLAs
- Sample-then-correct > sample-then-select (+7pp on LIBERO object)
- Observation features > conformal features for correction conditioning (honest negative)
- Correction magnitude control is critical and previously unrecognized

---

## Appendix (supplementary)
- Per-task breakdown tables (all 10 tasks × all methods)
- CRM training details (architecture, hyperparameters, training data)
- Conformal prediction background (CGS, nonconformity scores)
- Additional magnitude sweep results
- Compute analysis (K=10 overhead, CRM inference time)

1	# Ablation: K-Value Sweep
2	
3	We sweep the number of VLA samples K ∈ {2, 10, 20} drawn from the flow-matching policy and held fixed at the obs_only CRM head (ε = 0.2). The VLA-only K=1 baseline is reported for reference. Increasing K beyond 2 yields no measurable success-rate gain on either suite, supporting our adaptive K=2 configuration (Plan A) as Pareto-optimal in compute.
4	
5	**Table A: Effect of K on closed-loop success rate (mean ± std across seeds).**
6	
7	| K | Object SR (%) | Spatial SR (%) | n_seeds | Object exp_ids | Spatial exp_ids |
8	|---|--------------:|---------------:|--------:|----------------|-----------------|
9	| 1 (VLA-only) | 10.8 ± 1.3 | 29.4 ± 1.5 | ≥4 / ≥4 | `eval-vla-only-object-*` | `eval-pi05-vla-only-spatial-*` |
10	| 2 (Plan A, adaptive) | **18.3 ± 2.1** | **35.0 ± 1.0** | 3 / 3 | `eval-plan-a-object-seed{42,43,44}` | `eval-plan-a-spatial-seed{42,43,44}` |
11	| 10 | 16.8 ± 1.8 | 34.5 ± 1.5 | ≥3 / ≥3 | obs_only norm0.2 seed pool | spatial obs_only seed pool |
12	| 20 | 18.8 ± 1.0 | 34.3 ± 0.6 | 4 / 3 | `eval-k20-obs-only-object-seed{42,43,44,45}` | `eval-k20-obs-only-spatial-seed{42,43,44}` |
13	
14	Per-seed K=20 raw numbers (Object): 20%, 18%, 18%, 19%. Per-seed K=20 raw (Spatial): 35%, 34%, 34%. All K=20 runs use the same CRM checkpoint (`obs_only_K10_eps02_default`) and differ only in the number of candidate actions resampled at inference.
15	
16	**Diminishing returns beyond K=2.** Moving from K=1 → K=2 captures the bulk of the gain on both benchmarks (+7.5pp Object, +5.6pp Spatial). Subsequent doublings of K provide no additional improvement: on Object, K=10 (16.8%) and K=20 (18.8%) bracket the K=2 mean (18.3%) within one standard deviation; on Spatial, the three K values lie within 0.7pp of one another (34.3-35.0%) and the K=20 standard deviation (0.6%) overlaps the K=2 and K=10 confidence ranges. The pattern is consistent with the obs_only CRM's correction signal being driven by the observation features rather than by candidate diversity — once two samples provide an uncertainty estimate sufficient to trigger correction, additional candidates are absorbed by the same correction head without measurable benefit.
17	
18	**Implication for compute–accuracy trade-off.** A single flow-matching forward pass dominates inference cost; K=20 requires 10× more VLA forwards than K=2 with no return on closed-loop SR. The adaptive K=2 configuration (Plan A) — which performs a second forward only when the pairwise L2 distance between the first two samples exceeds τ=P50=0.0749 — pays at most 2× VLA compute and triggers correction on roughly 84% of steps on Object and 98% on Spatial, while matching K=20 SR within noise. We therefore adopt K=2 (Plan A) as the default in all downstream experiments and recommend it as the operating point for deployment.

1	# Related Work
2	
3	## VLA Robustness and Inference-Time Adaptation
4	
5	Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have rapidly advanced general-purpose robot control by leveraging large-scale vision-language pretraining [Brohan et al., 2023; Kim et al., 2024]. Flow-matching architectures such as pi0 [Black et al., 2024] and SmolVLA [Shukor et al., 2025] achieve strong performance on standard benchmarks but remain brittle under distribution shift, as systematically documented by LIBERO-Plus [Fei et al., 2025] and LIBERO-PRO [Xu et al., 2025].
6	
7	Several lines of work address VLA robustness at *training time*. RobustVLA [Zhang et al., 2025] applies Jacobian and smoothness regularization via RL post-training. SRPO [Fei et al., 2025] uses self-referential policy optimization to reach 82.1% on LIBERO-Plus. DiG-Flow [Zhang et al., 2025] introduces representation-level discrepancy guidance. ACoT-VLA [AgibotTech, 2026] adds chain-of-thought reasoning to VLA action prediction. VLA-GSE [Jiang et al., 2026] employs parameter-efficient fine-tuning with specialized experts. AFIL [2026] leverages failure trajectories as negative guidance during training. These methods require modifying the VLA training pipeline; our work is complementary, operating purely at inference time on a frozen model.
8	
9	At *inference time*, the landscape is sparser. ReconVLA [Chen et al., 2026] applies conformal prediction to produce calibrated uncertainty estimates and selects the best action from K candidates — a pure sample-selection strategy. VLA-Pilot [2025] uses a multimodal LLM verifier with evolutionary diffusion optimization for zero-shot policy steering, but incurs 2.41s per step. SC-VLA [Li et al., 2026] performs online action refinement via sparse future state prediction and residual RL, requiring environment interaction. TT-VLA [Liu et al., 2026] adapts VLAs through test-time reinforcement learning with progress-based rewards. A2C2 [Sendai et al., 2025] proposes an asynchronous action chunk correction head — the closest architecture to our CRM, but trained jointly with the VLA rather than as a post-hoc module. SAFE [Gu et al., 2025] focuses on failure detection using internal VLA features and conformal prediction to determine *when* to intervene. Our work differs from all of the above by (1) operating on a fully frozen VLA with no environment interaction, (2) systematically comparing correction conditioning features, and (3) identifying correction magnitude as a critical factor.
10	
11	SnapFlow [Luan et al., 2026] takes the opposite computational trade-off — distilling multi-step flow matching into a single inference step — while we invest additional compute (K=10 samples + CRM correction) to improve robustness.
12	
13	## Conformal Prediction in Robotics
14	
15	Conformal prediction (CP) provides distribution-free coverage guarantees without distributional assumptions [Shafer & Vovk, 2008; Angelopoulos & Bates, 2023]. Extensions to non-exchangeable settings [Barber et al., 2023] and online adaptation via Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI) [Gibbs & Candès, 2021] enable deployment under the distribution shifts inherent in robot operation.
16	
17	In multivariate action spaces, Conformalized Gaussian Scoring (CGS) [Braun et al., 2025] provides Mahalanobis-based nonconformity scores respecting inter-dimensional correlations, which we adopt for sample selection. Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR) [Romano et al., 2019] offers per-dimension heteroscedastic coverage. Recent work explores alternatives: Fan and Sesia [2025] develop coordinate-wise standardization for tighter marginal intervals, and Klein et al. [2025] use optimal transport ordering for principled multivariate quantiles.
18	
19	Several works apply CP to robot planning and control. Zhao et al. [2024] use adaptive CP for uncertainty detection in high-DOF teleoperation at RSS 2024. Wang and Ning [2025] integrate CP into trajectory optimization loops with coverage guarantees. Zhou et al. [2025] combine ACP with control barrier functions for formally safe RL at ICRA 2025. Gonzales et al. [2026] pair conformal risk control with CBFs for human-robot interaction safety. Lekeufack et al. [2024] develop conformal decision theory for calibrated autonomous decisions. In the CP-for-robotics literature, CLAPS [2025] extends CP to Lie group configuration spaces, and LCP [2025] learns context-aware nonconformity functions for robot planning.
20	
21	A distinct thread uses CP for *downstream decision-making* rather than coverage: Jin and Candès [2023] use conformal p-values for selection with FDR control, and Huang et al. [2023] deploy CP in learned feature spaces. SafeDiffCon [2025] uses CP uncertainty quantiles to guide diffusion-based control at ICML 2025. Yuan et al. [2026] calibrate VLM+policy composition for strategy selection (act/ask/learn) using CP. Our work connects to this thread: we use conformal scores for sample selection, then investigate whether conformal statistics can additionally serve as conditioning features for learned correction — finding, surprisingly, that they cannot.
22	
23	The emerging area of VLA-specific uncertainty quantification provides further context. Zollo and Zemel [2025] present the first systematic calibration study for VLAs, introducing prompt ensembles and action-wise Platt scaling. Tang et al. [2026] identify the "averaging trap" in VLA uncertainty where mean aggregation dilutes critical signals. Xing et al. [2026] propose single-pass uncertainty via velocity divergence in flow matching models. Valle et al. [2025] establish evaluation metrics for VLA uncertainty. These works focus on *measuring* uncertainty; we focus on *acting on it* through learned correction.
24	
25	## Residual Correction and Learned Action Refinement
26	
27	Residual policy learning [Silver et al., 2018] establishes the framework of learning a correction on top of a base controller, with bounded corrections shown to preserve stability [Johannink et al., 2019]. This paradigm has been extended to VLA settings: PLD [Xiao et al., 2026] applies residual RL with scheduled magnitude bounds on LIBERO at ICLR 2026, and DAWN [Ma et al., 2026] analyzes scale mismatch between base policy and residual in value estimation. DRC [Pan et al., 2025] introduces temporal decay of correction magnitude over episodes. TRANSIC [Jiang et al., 2024] demonstrates that ungated residual corrections lead to model collapse, motivating gated correction mechanisms — closely related to our finding that unbounded correction magnitude (norm=1.42) yields catastrophic 0% success rate.

29	A separate line of supervised (non-RL) correction includes DAgger [Ross et al., 2011], which reduces compounding error via iterative expert corrections, and its variants: CR-DAgger [Cai et al., 2025] learns compliant residual corrections from human interventions, and RaC [2025] scales recovery and correction from human intervention data. Reactive Diffusion Policy [Xue et al., 2025] uses a two-level slow-fast architecture with supervised fast correction. DART [Laskey et al., 2017] injects optimized noise for compounding error robustness without online interaction. 30

Dodeja and Schmeckpeper [2025] show that base policy uncertainty can focus residual RL exploration on low-confidence regions. # Related Work

## VLA Robustness and Inference-Time Adaptation

Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have rapidly advanced general-purpose robot control by leveraging large-scale vision-language pretraining [Brohan et al., 2023; Kim et al., 2024]. Flow-matching architectures such as pi0 [Black et al., 2024] and SmolVLA [Shukor et al., 2025] achieve strong performance on standard benchmarks but remain brittle under distribution shift, as systematically documented by LIBERO-Plus [Fei et al., 2025] and LIBERO-PRO [Xu et al., 2025].

Several lines of work address VLA robustness at *training time*. RobustVLA [Zhang et al., 2025] applies Jacobian and smoothness regularization via RL post-training. SRPO [Fei et al., 2025] uses self-referential policy optimization to reach 82.1% on LIBERO-Plus. DiG-Flow [Zhang et al., 2025] introduces representation-level discrepancy guidance. ACoT-VLA [AgibotTech, 2026] adds chain-of-thought reasoning to VLA action prediction. VLA-GSE [Jiang et al., 2026] employs parameter-efficient fine-tuning with specialized experts. AFIL [2026] leverages failure trajectories as negative guidance during training. These methods require modifying the VLA training pipeline; our work is complementary, operating purely at inference time on a frozen model.

At *inference time*, the landscape is sparser. ReconVLA [Chen et al., 2026] applies conformal prediction to produce calibrated uncertainty estimates and selects the best action from K candidates — a pure sample-selection strategy. VLA-Pilot [2025] uses a multimodal LLM verifier with evolutionary diffusion optimization for zero-shot policy steering, but incurs 2.41s per step. SC-VLA [Li et al., 2026] performs online action refinement via sparse future state prediction and residual RL, requiring environment interaction. TT-VLA [Liu et al., 2026] adapts VLAs through test-time reinforcement learning with progress-based rewards. A2C2 [Sendai et al., 2025] proposes an asynchronous action chunk correction head — the closest architecture to our CRM, but trained jointly with the VLA rather than as a post-hoc module. SAFE [Gu et al., 2025] focuses on failure detection using internal VLA features and conformal prediction to determine *when* to intervene. Our work differs from all of the above by (1) operating on a fully frozen VLA with no environment interaction, (2) systematically comparing correction conditioning features, and (3) identifying correction magnitude as a critical factor.

SnapFlow [Luan et al., 2026] takes the opposite computational trade-off — distilling multi-step flow matching into a single inference step — while we invest additional compute (K=10 samples + CRM correction) to improve robustness.

## Conformal Prediction in Robotics

Conformal prediction (CP) provides distribution-free coverage guarantees without distributional assumptions [Shafer & Vovk, 2008; Angelopoulos & Bates, 2023]. Extensions to non-exchangeable settings [Barber et al., 2023] and online adaptation via Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI) [Gibbs & Candès, 2021] enable deployment under the distribution shifts inherent in robot operation.

In multivariate action spaces, Conformalized Gaussian Scoring (CGS) [Braun et al., 2025] provides Mahalanobis-based nonconformity scores respecting inter-dimensional correlations, which we adopt for sample selection. Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR) [Romano et al., 2019] offers per-dimension heteroscedastic coverage. Recent work explores alternatives: Fan and Sesia [2025] develop coordinate-wise standardization for tighter marginal intervals, and Klein et al. [2025] use optimal transport ordering for principled multivariate quantiles.

Several works apply CP to robot planning and control. Zhao et al. [2024] use adaptive CP for uncertainty detection in high-DOF teleoperation at RSS 2024. Wang and Ning [2025] integrate CP into trajectory optimization loops with coverage guarantees. Zhou et al. [2025] combine ACP with control barrier functions for formally safe RL at ICRA 2025. Gonzales et al. [2026] pair conformal risk control with CBFs for human-robot interaction safety. Lekeufack et al. [2024] develop conformal decision theory for calibrated autonomous decisions. In the CP-for-robotics literature, CLAPS [2025] extends CP to Lie group configuration spaces, and LCP [2025] learns context-aware nonconformity functions for robot planning.

A distinct thread uses CP for *downstream decision-making* rather than coverage: Jin and Candès [2023] use conformal p-values for selection with FDR control, and Huang et al. [2023] deploy CP in learned feature spaces. SafeDiffCon [2025] uses CP uncertainty quantiles to guide diffusion-based control at ICML 2025. Yuan et al. [2026] calibrate VLM+policy composition for strategy selection (act/ask/learn) using CP. Our work connects to this thread: we use conformal scores for sample selection, then investigate whether conformal statistics can additionally serve as conditioning features for learned correction — finding, surprisingly, that they cannot.

The emerging area of VLA-specific uncertainty quantification provides further context. Zollo and Zemel [2025] present the first systematic calibration study for VLAs, introducing prompt ensembles and action-wise Platt scaling. Tang et al. [2026] identify the "averaging trap" in VLA uncertainty where mean aggregation dilutes critical signals. Xing et al. [2026] propose single-pass uncertainty via velocity divergence in flow matching models. Valle et al. [2025] establish evaluation metrics for VLA uncertainty. These works focus on *measuring* uncertainty; we focus on *acting on it* through learned correction.

## Residual Correction and Learned Action Refinement

Residual policy learning [Silver et al., 2018] establishes the framework of learning a correction on top of a base controller, with bounded corrections shown to preserve stability [Johannink et al., 2019]. This paradigm has been extended to VLA settings: PLD [Xiao et al., 2026] applies residual RL with scheduled magnitude bounds on LIBERO at ICLR 2026, and DAWN [Ma et al., 2026] analyzes scale mismatch between base policy and residual in value estimation. DRC [Pan et al., 2025] introduces temporal decay of correction magnitude over episodes. TRANSIC [Jiang et al., 2024] demonstrates that ungated residual corrections lead to model collapse, motivating gated correction mechanisms — closely related to our finding that unbounded correction magnitude (norm=1.42) yields catastrophic 0% success rate.

A separate line of supervised (non-RL) correction includes DAgger [Ross et al., 2011], which reduces compounding error via iterative expert corrections, and its variants: CR-DAgger [Cai et al., 2025] learns compliant residual corrections from human interventions, and RaC [2025] scales recovery and correction from human intervention data. Reactive Diffusion Policy [Xue et al., 2025] uses a two-level slow-fast architecture with supervised fast correction. DART [Laskey et al., 2017] injects optimized noise for compounding error robustness without online interaction. Our CRM follows the supervised correction paradigm — trained offline via L2 regression on calibration data — but uniquely conditions on VLA observation features and constrains correction magnitude, avoiding the RL training loops required by PLD, SC-VLA, and DAWN.

The question of *what to condition corrections on* is underexplored. Most residual methods condition on the full state or observation. Dodeja and Schmeckpeper [2025] show that base policy uncertainty can focus residual RL exploration on low-confidence regions. TRACE [Fang et al., 2026] defines scalar nonconformity scores via transport alignment in flow matching, avoiding per-dimension decomposition. Our systematic ablation across conditioning features — observation embeddings, per-DOF conformal statistics, and scalar conformal scores — reveals that richer statistical features do not translate to better correction, challenging the intuition that more informative conditioning is always beneficial.

2	\section{Experiments}
3	\label{sec:experiments}
4	
5	\looseness=-1 We evaluate ACR-VLA on SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} (0.4B) across four LIBERO~\cite{liu2023libero} task suites, comparing five methods that isolate the contributions of selection, correction, and adaptive gating. We ask: (i)~does adaptive gating produce positive improvements where unconditional correction and selection-only approaches fail? (ii)~what is the computational cost of the uncertainty probe?
6	
7	\subsection{Setup}
8	\label{sec:exp_setup}
9	
10	\paragraph{Benchmarks.}
11	We use all four LIBERO suites: Spatial (10 tasks, spatial reasoning), Object (10 tasks, novel object instances), Goal (10 tasks, goal specification), and Long (10 tasks, long-horizon manipulation). Each task is evaluated over 20 rollouts (max 300 steps, 200 per suite); success is binary.
12	
13	\paragraph{Base VLA.}
14	\looseness=-1 SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} (0.4B parameters, flow matching) uses dual-camera RGB ($256{\times}256$), 8D proprioceptive state, and produces 7D actions (6D pose + 1D gripper, thresholded separately). We additionally report $\pi_{0.5}$~\cite{black2024pi0} (3.6B) baselines and OpenVLA-OFT~\cite{kim2024openvla} (7B) boundary analysis in Section~\ref{sec:cross_vla}.
15	
16	\paragraph{Methods.}
17	All methods use the same frozen SmolVLA; no VLA weights are modified:
18	\begin{itemize}[nosep]
19	  \item \textbf{VLA-only} ($K{=}1$): single forward pass, no correction.
20	  \item \textbf{CRM always-on} ($K{=}10$, $\varepsilon{=}0.05$): argmin selection + unconditional CRM correction at every step. Uses a conservative norm bound ($\varepsilon{=}0.05$) to limit overcorrection.
21	  \item \textbf{$K{=}10$ argmin}~\cite{chen2026reconvla} ($K{=}10$): argmin-to-centroid selection over 10 samples, no learned correction. Represents the selection-only approach.
22	  \item \textbf{ACR-VLA} ($K{=}2$, $\varepsilon{=}0.2$, $\tau{=}0.25$): the proposed adaptive pipeline (Section~\ref{sec:adaptive_k_method}). CRM correction applied only when $d_2 > \tau$.
23	  \item \textbf{$K{=}2$ mean}: centroid of two samples, no CRM. Isolates the multi-sampling effect.
24	\end{itemize}
25	
26	\paragraph{CRM training.}
27	\looseness=-1 The CRM (${\sim}$327K parameters) is trained on LIBERO demonstrations with 10 demos per task, $K{=}10$ forward passes each (Adam $\mathrm{lr}{=}10^{-3}$, batch 32, 50 epochs, $\varepsilon{=}0.2$ for adaptive / $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ for always-on). For Spatial, Object, and Goal, the CRM is trained on three suites (30 tasks, ${\sim}$168K samples); for Long, we use a CRM trained on all four suites (40 tasks, ${\sim}$224K samples) to include Long-horizon demonstrations in the training distribution.
28	
29	\paragraph{Statistics.}
30	We report mean $\pm$ std; seed count is superscripted. With $n \leq 3$ seeds per condition, we report effect sizes and directional consistency rather than statistical significance tests.
31	
32	\subsection{Main Results}
33	\label{sec:main_results}
34	
35	\begin{table}[t]
